subject: spatial mark resight activity center sampler for unmarked individuals

messages.author: 2c49652a5796ed9c
messages.subject: spatial mark resight activity center sampler for unmarked individuals
parts:
I recently compared my R-based sampler for various spatial mark resight models to NIMBLE analogs and noticed the point estimates differed slightly. My first intuition is that the activity center sampler chosen by NIMBLE was not adequate and I'm very confident that is the case. I'm wondering if there is a good solution.

In the spatial mark resight scenario I am considering, a known subset of the population of N individuals is marked so that we can identify them upon capture. So the population is divided into a marked component of known size and an unknown component of unknown size. The marked individuals are generally treated the same as in a regular spatial capture-recapture problem and the unmarked samples can be treated in one of two ways. First, we can use the likelihood for the unmarked capture history summed over individuals (we don't know which samples belong to which individuals). Second, we can probabilistically reconstruct the unmarked individual capture history. This second option is generally unnecessary, but the first option cannot be used when you have samples where you cannot tell what their marked status is (could belong to marked or unmarked individuals). Further, when you have samples that you know are from marked individuals, but you don't know which one, the marked individual capture history needs to be probabilistically reconstructed.

Focusing on the unmarked individuals here, on each iteration of the MCMC algorithm, the individual each sample is associated with is proposed to change--samples are being probabilistically reallocated among the M activity centers. So sometimes one specific activity center is allocated 1 or more samples, and sometimes it is not. This makes tuning the activity center sampler difficult. If you use an adaptive tuning, it is largely tuned for when an activity center is allocated 0 samples, because this is the most common state when M is adequate. But then, when a sample is allocated to the activity center, the RW step is too large and it tends to not move. This prevents the activity centers from adjusting once they are allocated a sample.

The problem described above causes convergence to sometimes be extremely slow and the acceptance rates for the activity centers look good because they largely reflect the acceptance rates when no samples are assigned to an activity center. Therefore, the problem is difficult for the naive user to diagnose.

In my R-based sampler, I have just been using my intuition to set a single acceptance rate and it converges relatively quickly. I can replace the NIMBLE-selected sampler with the same sampler I use in R, but the average user will not know what to set the proposal parameter to for their data set. I'm wondering if there is a more foolproof solution for NIMBLE that will automatically select settings that will work for this model. Ideally, we would have an algorithm that will tune the activity center acceptance rates for condition 1 - s[i] is allocated 1 or more samples, condition 2 - s[i] is allocated 0 samples and z[i]=1, and condition 3, is allocated 0 samples and z[i]=0.

You can see the behavior in the attached files. In "smix1", you see the behavior we want. The activity center (just the x dimension plotted here) moves randomly around the state space until a sample is allocated to it, then it explores a very small area of the state space because it is linked to a specific trap. Then eventually, the sample moves to another activity center and so on. In "smix2", you can see a few places where the s[i] sampler gets stuck. Here, what happens is that it is more quickly reallocated to another activity center because it cannot move and better adjust it's position relative to the sample allocated to it.

Any thoughts on a NIMBLE sampler we can use that does not require the user to set a single proposal parameter that is appropriate for each data set? The sampler below works fine (I got it from Nathan Hostetter), but the user must set the proposal parameter appropriately.

myActivityCenterSampler <- nimbleFunction(
  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
    # Defined stuff
    ind<-control$ind     # defined during the model call. probably a more elegant way to do this, but it works for now.
    scale<-0.50          # could make this adaptive (see examples at nimble's Git)
    xlim<-model$xlim
    ylim<-model$ylim
    calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
  },
 
  run = function() {
    # grab current value of z
    z.curr <- model$z[ind]
   
    ## If z==0 propose activity center and accept with probablity 1.0
    if(z.curr==0){
     
      # store proposal into model
      model$s[ind, 1:2] <<- c(runif(1, xlim[1], xlim[2]), runif(1, ylim[1], ylim[2]))
     
      # update dependencies
      model$calculate(calcNodes)
     
      # Accept candidate trajectory with probabliy 1.0 and keep the model and mvSaved objects consistent
      copy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
     
    }#if z.curr==0
   
    ## If z==1 propose activity center and use MH update to accept/reject
    if(z.curr==1){
     
      # initial model logProb
      model_lp_initial <- model$getLogProb(calcNodes)
     
      # generate candidate trajectory conditional on current trajectory
      ## this could be more efficient, including adapting the proposal scale parameter
      ## see nimble examples on Git
     
      # store proposal into model
      #truncated normal
      sx <- qnorm(runif(1, pnorm(xlim[1], model$s[ind, 1], sd=scale), pnorm(xlim[2], model$s[ind, 1], sd=scale)), model$s[ind, 1], sd=scale)
      sy <- qnorm(runif(1, pnorm(ylim[1], model$s[ind, 2], sd=scale), pnorm(ylim[2], model$s[ind, 2], sd=scale)), model$s[ind, 2], sd=scale)
      model$s[ind, 1:2] <<- c(sx, sy)
     
      # proposal could be anything, as long as non-symmetric proposals are accounted for in the MH step.
      #model$s[ind, 1:2] <<- c(runif(1, xlim[1], xlim[2]), runif(1, ylim[1], ylim[2]))
     
      # proposal model logProb
      model_lp_proposed <- model$calculate(calcNodes)
     
      # log-Metropolis-Hastings ratio
      log_MH_ratio <- model_lp_proposed - model_lp_initial
      # Metropolis-Hastings step: determine whether or
      # not to accept the newly proposed value
      accept <- decide(log_MH_ratio)
      if(accept) {
        copy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
      } else {
        copy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
      }
    }#z==1
   
  },
  methods = list( reset = function () {} )
)

Ben

parts: Actually, a decent solution in this case is for the user to supply one proposal parameter for the activity centers and make sure the acceptance rates for the marked individuals is OK. Absent a major model specification, the unmarked activity center acceptance rates will necessarily be at least decent. But that rule of thumb isn't available for similar models with no marked individuals. In either case, we shouldn't let nimble select or tune it.

I'm just wondering if there is a way to leverage NIMBLE functionality so that the user does not need to be an expert on activity center mixing in these models. The only idea I have is perhaps NIMBLE can tune 2 proposal parameters for you in a custom update and you apply one to the situation where z[i]=1 and sum(y[i,]=0) and another to the situation where z[i]=1 and sum(y[i,]>0). z[i]=0 are then proposed from the prior. It seems unlikely this would be possible, but who knows!

parts:
Hi Ben,

Sorry this fell by the wayside for a while.

I can offer several suggestions.

One way to simplify this for other users would be to write a function that manages the sampler assignments.  That eases the burden of learning nimble if you want to share what you develop with others.  

For the samplers themselves, here are a few ideas. 

It's possible to write one "sampler" (i.e. item on the sampler list) that contains many actual samplers (i.e. nimbleFunctions that do an MCMC update).  The many samplers can then share tuning parameter(s).  This would allow them to tune to average acceptance rate across all activity centers, not each separately.  

I didn't follow what you meant by "a single, non-adaptive random walk sampler for z[i]=1 individuals."  Each sampler object targets one node (or nodes).  Maybe you meant what I just tried to describe?

On your idea of having sampler behavior depend on system state(s): In general, one must be careful about this, but I think your specific suggestion would be valid.  If the proposal scale for updating z is made to depend on the value of z, the sampler will not be valid unless care is taken to make the ratio of backward/forward proposal densities in the acceptance probability correct.  But you are suggesting that the proposal scale for updating one value depends on a different parameter that would not change.  That should be valid.

-Perry

Following up on this many months later. I'm can't figure out how to do 2 things for a spatial capture-recapture type sampler. Both concern the activity center update, which I'm replacing with a custom update.

1. I want to get the dependencies for 1 activity center at a time, but c++ doesn't understand the "paste" command (in red below). This does work in R, which does know "paste".  Is there a way to extract the dependencies for one activity center at a time when specifying a single update for all activity centers (target is s[1;M,1;2])?

2. I'm unsure if I am successfully making this sampler adapt. I want it to adapt a single scale parameter for all activity centers, which is only used when each z[i]==1. I attempt to tell it to adapt when replacing the sampler (below in blue), but getScaleHistory() does not return anything, while it does for RW samplers that are not custom (following nimble manual section 7.5.2). Also, I'm unsure how nimble counts acceptances. Will it count them for z[i]==0 updates? I don't want that to happen.

Any help would be much appreciated!

Ben

  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
    # Defined stuff

scale<-1  
    xlim<-control$xlim
    ylim<-control$ylim
    M<-control$M

},
 
  run = function() {
    # grab current value of z

z <- model$z
    for(i in 1:M){
      browser()
      calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(paste("s[",i,",1:2]"))
      ## If z==0 propose activity center and accept with probability 1.0
      if(z[i]==0){
# store proposal into model

model$s[i, 1:2] <<- c(runif(1, xlim[1], xlim[2]), runif(1, ylim[1], ylim[2]))
       
        # update dependencies
        model$calculate(calcNodes)
       
        # Accept candidate trajectory with probability 1.0 and keep the model and mvSaved objects consistent
copy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
}else{#z.curr[i]==1

# initial model logProb
        model_lp_initial <- model$getLogProb(calcNodes)

#truncated normal proposal
        sx <- qnorm(runif(1, pnorm(xlim[1], model$s[i, 1], sd=scale), pnorm(xlim[2], model$s[i, 1], sd=scale)), model$s[i, 1], sd=scale)
        sy <- qnorm(runif(1, pnorm(ylim[1], model$s[i, 2], sd=scale), pnorm(ylim[2], model$s[i, 2], sd=scale)), model$s[i, 2], sd=scale)
        model$s[i, 1:2] <<- c(sx, sy)

# proposal model logProb
        model_lp_proposed <- model$calculate(calcNodes)
       
        # log-Metropolis-Hastings ratio
        log_MH_ratio <- model_lp_proposed - model_lp_initial
        # Metropolis-Hastings step: determine whether or
        # not to accept the newly proposed value

jump <- decide(log_MH_ratio)
        if(jump) {

copy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
        } else {
          copy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
        }
       
      }#z==1
    }
  },
  methods = list( reset = function () {} )
)

conf$removeSampler("s")
conf$addSampler(target = paste(paste("s[1:",M,",1:2]"),sep=""),
                    type = 'myActivityCenterSampler',control = list(xlim=xlims,ylim=ylims,M=M,
                            adaptive=TRUE, adaptInterval=100), #there has to be a better way to assign this stuff
                    silent = TRUE)

Ben, this is extremely hasty because I'm off in just 15 minutes, but here's the gist.

1. The modified code below shows (at least how I would) do what you're trying to do.  Short answer, you can't use "paste" in compiled execution, all node names, and sets of nodes, must be predefined in setup code.  Here we use a nimbleFunctionList.  See the modifications throughout.  Caution.  I have not run, or executed this code, so be very wary of typos, or minor errors, there certainly are some.

2. This is no "bigger system for sampler adaptation".  It's sampler-by-sampler. Everything the RW sampler does to adapt is in the RW sampler code, see on GitHub.  Just supplying adaptive=TRUE, and adaptItnerval in the control list won't do anything.  To adapt the scale parameter, you'll need to include custom code (in the sampler) to do that.  You might follow the code in RW sampler as a model, or in your case, record the total number of successful (and failed) transitions, and use that.  I'd look at the sampler_RW code, and everything in there having to do with adaptation, and go from there.

Good luck.  Modified code below.

    name = 'myActivityCenterSampler_helperBASE',
    methods = list(
        calc = function() { returnType(double()) },
        setValue = function(newValue = double(1)) { },
        copyToMVsaved = function() { },
        copyToModel = function() { },
        getLP = function() { returnType(double()) }
    )
)

On Sun, Aug 9, 2020 at 5:24 PM baug...@vt.edu <baug...@vt.edu> wrote:

Following up on this many months later. I'm can't figure out how to do 2 things for a spatial capture-recapture type sampler. Both concern the activity center update, which I'm replacing with a custom update.

1. I want to get the dependencies for 1 activity center at a time, but c++ doesn't understand the "paste" command (in red below). This does work in R, which does know "paste".  Is there a way to extract the dependencies for one activity center at a time when specifying a single update for all activity centers (target is s[1;M,1;2])?

2. I'm unsure if I am successfully making this sampler adapt. I want it to adapt a single scale parameter for all activity centers, which is only used when each z[i]==1. I attempt to tell it to adapt when replacing the sampler (below in blue), but getScaleHistory() does not return anything, while it does for RW samplers that are not custom (following nimble manual section 7.5.2). Also, I'm unsure how nimble counts acceptances. Will it count them for z[i]==0 updates? I don't want that to happen.

Any help would be much appreciated!

Ben


myActivityCenterSampler <- nimbleFunction(
  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
    # Defined stuff
    scale<-1  
    xlim<-control$xlim
    ylim<-control$ylim
    M<-control$M

  },
 
  run = function() {
    # grab current value of z
    z <- model$z
    for(i in 1:M){
      browser()
      calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(paste("s[",i,",1:2]"))
      ## If z==0 propose activity center and accept with probability 1.0
      if(z[i]==0){
       
        # store proposal into model
        model$s[i, 1:2] <<- c(runif(1, xlim[1], xlim[2]), runif(1, ylim[1], ylim[2]))
       
        # update dependencies
        model$calculate(calcNodes)
       
        # Accept candidate trajectory with probability 1.0 and keep the model and mvSaved objects consistent
        copy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
       
      }else{#z.curr[i]==1
       
        # initial model logProb
        model_lp_initial <- model$getLogProb(calcNodes)

        #truncated normal proposal
        sx <- qnorm(runif(1, pnorm(xlim[1], model$s[i, 1], sd=scale), pnorm(xlim[2], model$s[i, 1], sd=scale)), model$s[i, 1], sd=scale)
        sy <- qnorm(runif(1, pnorm(ylim[1], model$s[i, 2], sd=scale), pnorm(ylim[2], model$s[i, 2], sd=scale)), model$s[i, 2], sd=scale)
        model$s[i, 1:2] <<- c(sx, sy)
       
       
        # proposal model logProb
        model_lp_proposed <- model$calculate(calcNodes)
       
        # log-Metropolis-Hastings ratio
        log_MH_ratio <- model_lp_proposed - model_lp_initial
        # Metropolis-Hastings step: determine whether or
        # not to accept the newly proposed value
        jump <- decide(log_MH_ratio)
        if(jump) {
          copy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
        } else {
          copy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
        }
       
      }#z==1
    }
  },
  methods = list( reset = function () {} )
)


conf$removeSampler("s")
conf$addSampler(target = paste(paste("s[1:",M,",1:2]"),sep=""),
                    type = 'myActivityCenterSampler',control = list(xlim=xlims,ylim=ylims,M=M,
                            adaptive=TRUE, adaptInterval=100), #there has to be a better way to assign this stuff
                    silent = TRUE)

Hi Ben,

Sorry this fell by the wayside for a while.

I can offer several suggestions.

One way to simplify this for other users would be to write a function that manages the sampler assignments.  That eases the burden of learning nimble if you want to share what you develop with others.  

For the samplers themselves, here are a few ideas. 

It's possible to write one "sampler" (i.e. item on the sampler list) that contains many actual samplers (i.e. nimbleFunctions that do an MCMC update).  The many samplers can then share tuning parameter(s).  This would allow them to tune to average acceptance rate across all activity centers, not each separately.  

I didn't follow what you meant by "a single, non-adaptive random walk sampler for z[i]=1 individuals."  Each sampler object targets one node (or nodes).  Maybe you meant what I just tried to describe?

-Perry
